To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the selectivity of acrolein hydrogenation by nickel–titanium alloy catalysts was improved by alloying, and this was due to the retardation of the hydrogenation of the formyI group by the alloying.
the Ni28Ti72 catalyst is a selective catalyst for the hydrogenation reaction of acrolein, which is a precursor to propionaldehyde.
Ni28Ti72 catalysts have a high selectivitiy for the hydrogenation acrolein to propanaldehyde, while supported Ni and Ni nanoparticles are less selective.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the selective hydrogenation of acetylene, acrolein and crotonaldehyde by Ni–Ti alloy catalysts, and the effects of the electronic and geometric structures of Ni–Ti alloy on the hydrogenation activity and selectivity are discussed.
the hydrogenation of the formy group of acrolein and the effect of alloying on the selectivity of hydrogenation.
the development of a novel Ni–Ti alloy catalyst which has a high selectivity to propionaldehyde by the hydrogenation of a single C=C double bond.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the selectivity for propionaldehyde formation is determined by the electronic effect, whereas the rate is controlled by the geometric effect.
the selectivity of Ni28Ti72 is caused by the retardation of the hydrogenation of the formy group by the electronic effect.
the selectivity to propionaldehyde is enhanced by the electronic effect of alloying and by the formation of Ni–Ti alloy particles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electronic effect is a major factor for the selectivity of the hydrogenation of the formy1 group in acrolein.
a Ni–Ti alloy catalyst with a high selectivity is not only a good candidate for hydrogenation of acrylates, but also for hydrogenation of formyl groups.
the hydrogenation of formyl group is retarded by alloying with titanium and the hydrogenation of carbon-carbon double bonds is accelerated by alloying.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Ni28Ti72 is the most selective hydrogenation catalyst for the production of propionaldehyde from acrolein.
the selectivity of acrolein hydrogenation is strongly dependent upon the electronic effect of the alloy catalysts, and that the selectivity is improved by alloying with a late transition metal.
the selectivity for the formyl group can be improved by alloying with a non-noble metal.
